data.why: The repo ships no example FASTA/Newick/matrix/PDB files (only a compressed demo-board blob in public/mseaboard-example.txt), so a small matched set of 6-taxon nucleotide MSA, Newick tree, PHYLIP-style distance matrix, GC-content table, and a 10-residue synthetic PDB backbone were written so a scientist can exercise cross-panel linking (MSA<->tree<->matrix<->structure) with realistic edge cases (identical sequence pair, an ambiguous 'N' base, a 6nt deletion/gap, and a divergent outlier taxon).

goals: Load a multiple sequence alignment and visually inspect conservation, gaps, and an ambiguous base call across taxa
Link an MSA panel to a phylogenetic tree panel so hovering a sequence highlights its corresponding leaf and vice versa
Build a pairwise distance matrix from the MSA (or from the tree's patristic distances) and open it as a linked heatmap to compare substitution patterns against the tree topology
Reconstruct a phylogenetic tree directly from the MSA using the embedded FastME engine and compare it to a reference tree
Load a 3D protein structure and link it to its derived contact map / chain sequence to relate structural proximity to sequence or alignment columns
Extract a subset of sequences or a subtree, or prune outlier taxa, to produce a cleaned-up filtered panel for further comparison

review.summary: The tree describes the tool well as a canvas of linked alignment, tree, matrix, data and structure panels, with derived analyses that spawn new linked panels. Most cited screens show what the nodes say. It still needs fixes before filing: one citation shows the wrong FastME settings, the heatmap-to-tree link is shown only by a link dot, two plan goals (structure-to-alignment linking and comparing the inferred tree with the reference) are missing, and several tasks were never confirmed by the replay.
